newsitem.title: USA: Judge blocks bondholders from ousting Marvel board.
newsitem.headline: Judge blocks bondholders from ousting Marvel board.

text.p: A U.S. Bankruptcy Court Judge granted a temporary restraining order that prevents a bondholder group, led by Carl Icahn, from taking control of the board of directors of Marvel Entertainment Group Inc, said officials representing bondholders and Marvel.
"Today's court ruling means that Marvel and the banks are free to explore all options to protect the company's future," said a Marvel spokesman. He declined further comment.
Bondholders planned to replace Marvel's current board with their own slate of directors on March 25, after foreclosing on 80 million Marvel shares which collateralize their bonds.
The judge will allow bondholders to file a motion to seek relief from the restraining order or to appeal the decision, Marvel and bondholder officials confirmed.
A spokeswoman for the bondholders said only, "We will consider all of our options."
Judge Helen Balick, of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court of Delaware, presided over the hearing.
Balick is the same judge who had lifted an automatic stay last month that prevented bondholders from foreclosing on the Marvel common stock.
Court officials could not be reached.
